text: For vehicles with 12 V systems, the maximum allowed negative pulse amplitude of transient conducted emissions generated by the ESA shall be -100 V.
test_case: Verify that the negative transient peak measured per ISO 7637-2 does not exceed -100 V.
why: Transient emission limit for an ESA intended for a 12 V M1 vehicle.

text: For vehicles with 24 V systems, the maximum allowed positive pulse amplitude of transient conducted emissions generated by the ESA shall be +150 V.
test_case: Verify that the positive transient peak measured per ISO 7637-2 is ≤ +150 V.
why: Applies if the lamp ESA is intended for 24 V systems.

text: For vehicles with 24 V systems, the maximum allowed negative pulse amplitude of transient conducted emissions generated by the ESA shall be -450 V.
test_case: Verify that the negative transient peak measured per ISO 7637-2 does not exceed -450 V.
why: Applies if the lamp ESA is intended for 24 V systems.

text: For TEM cell testing, the ESA shall be tested with a test level of 75 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 200 MHz frequency range.
test_case: Perform the ISO 11452-3 TEM cell test at 75 V/m.
why: Table 2a immunity severity applicable to the ESA.

text: For BCI testing, the ESA shall be tested with a test level of 60 mA in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range.
test_case: Perform the ISO 11452-4 BCI test at 60 mA.
why: Table 2a immunity severity applicable to the ESA.

text: For ALSE testing, the ESA shall be tested with a test level of 30 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency range.
test_case: Perform the ISO 11452-2 ALSE test at 30 V/m from 80 to 2,000 MHz.
why: Table 2a immunity severity applicable to the ESA.

text: For ALSE testing, the ESA shall be tested with a test level of 10 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range.
test_case: Perform the ISO 11452-2 ALSE test at 10 V/m from 2,000 to 6,000 MHz.
why: Table 2a immunity severity applicable to the ESA.

text: For reverberation chamber testing, the ESA shall be tested with a test level of 7 V/m in over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range.
test_case: Perform the ISO 11452-11 reverberation test at 7 V/m from 2,000 to 6,000 MHz.
why: Table 2a immunity severity applicable to the ESA.

text: For BCI testing, the minimum test level over the whole 20 to 400 MHz frequency range shall be 50 mA.
test_case: Verify that the BCI current never falls below 50 mA.
why: Table 2b minimum immunity level applicable to the ESA.

text: For ALSE testing, the minimum test level over the whole 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency range shall be 25 V/m.
test_case: Verify that the ALSE field never falls below 25 V/m from 80 to 2,000 MHz.
why: Table 2b minimum immunity level applicable to the ESA.

text: For reverberation chamber testing, the minimum test level over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range shall be 6 V/m.
test_case: Verify that the reverberation field never falls below 6 V/m from 2,000 to 6,000 MHz.
why: Table 2b minimum immunity level applicable to the ESA.

text: For test pulse 3a, the ESA shall be tested at -112 V (12 V system) / -150 V (24 V system) for 1 h, meeting FPSC I for immunity related functions and III for functions not related to immunity related functions.
test_case: Apply pulse 3a for 1 h and verify status I.
why: Table 3b row applicable to the ESA.

text: For test pulse 3b, the ESA shall be tested at +75 V (12 V system) / +150 V (24 V system) for 1 h, meeting FPSC I for immunity related functions and III for functions not related to immunity related functions.
test_case: Apply pulse 3b for 1 h and verify status I.
why: Table 3b row applicable to the ESA.

text: When the conformity of an ESA taken from the series is being verified, the narrowband electromagnetic radiated emission levels measured shall not exceed by more than 4 dB (60 per cent) the reference limits prescribed in paragraph 6.6.2.1. (52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band, 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, 53 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band, measured according to Annex 8).
test_case: Measure narrowband emissions of a series sample per Annex 8 and check the result is at most limit + 4 dB.
why: This is the CoP narrowband emission tolerance for a production ESA.

text: If applicable, when the conformity of an ESA taken from the series is being verified, the ESA shall not exhibit any degradation relating to the direct control of the vehicle which could be observed by the driver or other road user when subjected to a field strength up to 80 per cent of the reference limits prescribed in paragraph 7.18.2.1.
test_case: Where charging-mode requirements apply, perform Annex 9 immunity tests at 80 % of the Table 19a/19b levels and check for degradation.
why: This conditional CoP immunity criterion applies to ESAs in charging mode.

text: If applicable, when the conformity of a component or STU taken from the series is being verified, the component shall show no degradation of performance of immunity related functions up to the levels given in paragraph 7.19.1.
test_case: Where charging-mode requirements apply, apply the Table 20 pulses and check the functional status classification.
why: This conditional CoP conducted immunity criterion applies to ESAs in charging mode.

text: The ESA shall withstand test pulse 2a according to ISO 7637-2 applied to the supply lines and to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulse 2a to the lamp supply and connected lines and check functional status.
why: Immunity to pulse 2a is required for ESAs on 12/24 V supply lines.

text: The ESA shall withstand test pulse 2b according to ISO 7637-2 applied to the supply lines and to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulse 2b to the lamp supply and connected lines and check functional status.
why: Immunity to pulse 2b is required for ESAs on 12/24 V supply lines.

text: The ESA shall withstand test pulse 3a according to ISO 7637-2 applied to the supply lines and to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulse 3a to the lamp supply and connected lines and check functional status.
why: Immunity to pulse 3a is required for ESAs on 12/24 V supply lines.

text: The ESA shall withstand test pulse 3b according to ISO 7637-2 applied to the supply lines and to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulse 3b to the lamp supply and connected lines and check functional status.
why: Immunity to pulse 3b is required for ESAs on 12/24 V supply lines.

text: The ESA shall withstand the starting profile according to ISO 16750-2 applied to the supply lines and to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.
test_case: Apply the ISO 16750-2 starting profile to the lamp supply lines and verify functional status.
why: The lamp ESA is fitted to M1 vehicles with 12/24 V starter motors and must tolerate cranking.

text: For the purposes of reducing the geometric visibility angles, the position of the lamp with regard to height above the ground shall be measured from the H plane.
test_case: Measure retro-reflector height from the H plane when applying the reduced downward angle.
why: Defines the height reference that conditions the reduced visibility angle for the retro-reflector.

text: For a required minimum value of 6∙10^-1 cd throughout the fields specified in Annexes 2 and 3, the measured value shall correspond to at least 4∙10^-1 cd (20 per cent equivalent) and 2∙10^-1 cd (30 per cent equivalent).
test_case: Photometric measurement at the relevant field points of production samples.
why: Table 12 row defining CoP minimum values for low-intensity field points.

text: For a required minimum value of 7∙10^-2 cd throughout the fields specified in Annexes 2 and 3, the measured value shall correspond to at least 5∙10^-2 cd (20 per cent equivalent) and 3∙10^-2 cd (30 per cent equivalent).
test_case: Photometric measurement at the relevant field points of production samples.
why: Table 12 row defining CoP minimum values for low-intensity field points.

text: For an optional rear position lamp (R1, R2) to be installed with the H-plane of the lamp at a mounting height of more than 2,100 mm, the minimum vertical angles shall be 5° above and 15° below.
test_case: If installed above 2,100 mm as an optional lamp, verify visibility at 5° up / 15° down.
why: Conditional case (note c) for the rear position lamp row.

text: For a stop lamp (S1, S2) mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm, reduced minimum horizontal angles of 20° inboard and 45° outboard may be used only below the H-plane.
test_case: Verify visibility below the H-plane down to 20° inboard / 45° outboard for mounting height below 750 mm.
why: Note a applies to the stop lamp when mounted below 750 mm.

text: For a stop lamp (S1, S2) to be installed with the H-plane of the lamp at a mounting height of less than 750 mm, the minimum vertical angles shall be 15° above and 5° below.
test_case: Verify visibility at 15° up / 5° down for the low-mounted installation.
why: Note b applies to the stop lamp when mounted below 750 mm.

text: For the stop lamp using light source technologies other than incandescent technology only (LED), the luminous intensities measured after 1 min and either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
test_case: Measure the stop lamp intensities at 1 min and at 30 min (or photometric stability) and verify against the min/max values (e.g. 60 to 185 cd on axis).
why: The stop lamp (P-02) is LED-based and falls under 'all other lamps'.

text: The luminous intensity distribution of the stop lamp shall, in addition to paragraph 1, comply at 0.2 seconds after switch ON, using HV as the reference coordinate.
test_case: Measure the HV intensity 0.2 s after switch ON and scale the distribution to verify compliance with the min/max values.
why: Table A8-1 row 'Stop' applies to stop lamp P-02.

text: The luminous intensity distribution of the reversing lamp shall, in addition to paragraph 1, comply at 0.2 seconds after switch ON, using HV as the reference coordinate.
test_case: Measure the HV intensity 0.2 s after switch ON and scale the distribution to verify compliance with the min/max values.
why: Table A8-1 row 'Reversing' applies to reversing lamp P-03.

text: For the measurement of the retro-reflector, the angular diameter of the measuring device shall be γ ≤ 10'.
test_case: Check the receiver aperture size and distance geometry.
why: Sets the measuring geometry that conditions the retro-reflector's compliance.

text: After the heat resistance test, no appreciable distortion of the retro-reflective device, and in particular of its optical component, must be visible.
test_case: Visually inspect the conditioned retro-reflector and its optical component for appreciable distortion.
why: This is the pass criterion for the heat test applied to the moulded plastics retro-reflector.

text: Immediately after completion of the corrosion test, the sample shall not show signs of excessive corrosion liable to impair the efficiency of the device.
test_case: Visually inspect the lamp and retro-reflector immediately after the saline mist test for excessive corrosion.
why: Pass/fail criterion for the retro-reflector combined with the rear lamp.

text: In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a stop lamp category S2 emitting more than the maximum value of category S1, the requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.
test_case: Simulate variable intensity control failure and measure stop lamp intensity against S1 steady limits.
why: [recall pass] Conditional failure-mode obligation for the stop lamp function if it is of category S2.

text: In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a stop lamp category S4 emitting more than the maximum value of category S3, the requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.
test_case: Simulate variable intensity control failure and measure stop lamp intensity against S3 steady limits.
why: [recall pass] Conditional failure-mode obligation for the stop lamp function if it is of category S4.

text: Where the rear position lamp of category R2 (variable) is marked "D" (paragraph 3.3.2.5.2.), its maximum luminous intensity shall not exceed 2.1∙10^1 cd.
test_case: Goniophotometer measurement of the maximum luminous intensity of the D-marked lamp.
why: [recall pass] Table 4 maximum-intensity limit for a D-marked R2 rear position lamp.

text: For a stop lamp of category S2 (variable), the standard light distribution shall be as defined in Figure A3-I.
test_case: Measure intensities at the Figure A3-I grid points and compare with the prescribed percentages.
why: [recall pass] Defines the required photometric distribution for an S2 stop lamp.

text: For a stop lamp of category S2 (variable), the angles of geometric visibility shall be as defined in Table A2-1.
test_case: Verify the visibility angles of the apparent surface against Table A2-1.
why: [recall pass] Defines the required visibility field for an S2 stop lamp.
